content_list.content_text: The tradition of physical comedy and slapstick inaugurated by Mack Sennett (1880-1960) was transformed into a verbal choreography in which one actor played the straight man while the other reeled off the jokes.

Jimmy Durante (1893-1980), for example, loved to scramble the order of his sentences, and W. C. Fields (1880-1946) - who improvised most of his own dialogue - constantly played with double meanings in films such as It's a Gift (1934).

information.contentText: A typical situation in the comic shorts of the duo Laurel and Hardy involves Stan and Ollie as workers who try, clumsily but with fierce dedication, to carry out a simple task. In The Music Box, their mission is to deliver a piano that a professor bought as a gift.

content_list.content_text: Hearing comedians talk was a new and bizarre experience, and some of them were better suited to the new medium than others. Resisting the trend toward talkies, Charlie Chaplin (1889-1977) released the silent City Lights (1931); the filmmaker would not make The Great Dictator (1940), his first film with dialogue, until 1940. Stan Laurel (1890-1965) and Oliver Hardy (1892-1957), the famous Laurel and Hardy, adapted immediately to the new era, but for other comedians the transition was not so easy.

quote.quote: Maybe you can suggest something. As a matter of fact, you do suggest something. To me, you suggest an ape.
quote.author: Rufus T. Firefly (Groucho Marx) in Duck Soup

content_list.content_text: Constrained by studio pressures and restrictions, Buster Keaton (1895-1966) found himself cut off from the artistic flourishes of his silent films and forced to settle for talkies such as Speak Easily (1932). Harold Lloyd's career went into decline and Harry Langdon soon fell into obscurity.

content_list.title: Double the Comedy
content_list.description:
When it comes to comedy, Laurel and Hardy remain the prototype of the yin-yang duo. However, their opposing personas were far more subtle and malleable than mere fat/thin or clown/straight-man dichotomies. Laurel's hallmarks were his effeminate, contemplative delicacy and a profound idiocy that sometimes gave way to bizarre bursts of cleverness. Ollie, for his part, was clumsy and pompous, but he also longed to appear gallant, as shown by his habit of bashfully twiddling his tie.

Much of the duo's genius lay in their mastery of the formalities of absurd comedy: the leisurely slowness of the double takes that punctuated their routines; the way Ollie stared in frustration at the camera; and the carefully staged episodes of their constant war with regular foil James Finlayson (1887-1953), in which the two would watch his explosions of rage before retaliating, always after exchanging a solemn nod.
content_list.credits: Summary based on the text by Simon Ward, published in the book "Cinema: The Whole Story" by Philip Kemp

content_list.content_text: With the addition of sound and recorded dialogue, comedies entered the realm of surrealism. Comic moments leaned toward the absurd, with Oliver Hardy's neck stretching impossibly in Way Out West (1937) and Harpo Marx making a candle burn at both ends in Horse Feathers (1932). This kind of fantastic situation foreshadowed the illogical world of the Looney Tunes.

Many of the comedians of the 1930s came from vaudeville and had honed their skills on stage before going into film. W. C. Fields's pool table routine in Six of a Kind (1934) was created during his years in the theater. Jack Benny was already a successful violinist and Jimmy Durante a jazz pianist - and both made use of those talents in their performances.

information.contentTitle: Scene with the mirror routine in Duck Soup (1933)
information.contentText: Harpo pretends to be Groucho's reflection, displaying extraordinary talent - although the brothers swap roles during the sketch. It is one of the most famous sequences in comedy film and is constantly imitated (in fact, the brothers stole it from Raymond Griffith).

content_list.content_text: Drawing on the perfectionism honed in stage rehearsals, Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy worked tirelessly on the two-minute dance sequence in Way Out West (1937). Some of these comedians created peculiar personas, defined by unmistakable characteristics, popular characters or distinctive traits, such as Jimmy Durante's big nose or skinny Stan in contrast to chubby Ollie. The two reached their creative peak during the 1930s, appearing in classics such as The Music Box (1932).

Perhaps the most brilliant comic creation of the period was the Marx Brothers. Of the three, Groucho was the most iconic figure, with his glasses, his cigar and his endless supply of biting wisecracks. The Marx Brothers brought their anarchic slapstick style from the stage to the screen, combining it with dialogue that had been too complex for the era when they performed in vaudeville.

information.contentText: The Three Stooges treat us to memorable slapstick situations in a hospital in the film Dizzy Doctors.

content_list.content_text: In films such as Duck Soup (1933), they defined the art of sarcastic comedy, and their influence on comedians such as Woody Allen (born 1935) is clear in the film Love and Death (1975), for example.

While the Marx Brothers were defining comic cinema, The Three Stooges, their fellow New Yorkers, emerged and became the cornerstone of American popular comedy. Curly, Larry and Moe had an extraordinarily prolific career together, starring (with some later lineup changes) in more than 200 shorts and feature films. The Three Stooges are best remembered for their slapstick style full of violence, often inflicted on one another, in films such as Dizzy Doctors (1937).
content_list.content_credits: Summary based on the text by Simon Ward, published in the book "Cinema: The Whole Story" by Philip Kemp

movies.title: Duck Soup
movies.overview: Rufus T. Firefly is named president/dictator of bankrupt Freedonia and declares war on neighboring Sylvania over the love of wealthy Mrs. Teasdale.

movies.title: The Music Box
movies.overview: The Laurel & Hardy Moving Co. have a challenging job on their hands (and backs): hauling a player piano up a monumental flight of stairs to Prof. von Schwarzenhoffen's house. Their task is complicated by a sassy nursemaid and, unbeknownst to them, the impatient Prof. von Schwarzenhoffen himself. But the biggest problem is the force of gravity, which repeatedly pulls the piano back down to the bottom of the stairs.

movies.title: Dizzy Doctors
movies.overview: The stooges get a job selling "Brighto", what they think is cleaning fluid. After ruining a cop's uniform and a new car, they discover Brighto is actually medicine. Taking their sales pitch to a hospital, they get into more trouble and must leave on the run when the head of hospital turns out to be the owner of the car they ruined.

movies.title: Horse Feathers
movies.overview: Quincy Adams Wagstaff, the new president of Huxley U, hires bumblers Baravelli and Pinky to help his school win the big football game against rival Darwin U.

movies.title: Modern Times
movies.overview: The Tramp struggles to live in modern industrial society with the help of a young homeless woman.

movies.title: The Great Dictator
movies.overview: Dictator Adenoid Hynkel tries to expand his empire while a poor Jewish barber tries to avoid persecution from Hynkel's regime.

movies.title: Way Out West
movies.overview: Stan and Ollie try to deliver the deed to a valuable gold mine to the daughter of a dead prospector. Unfortunately, the daughter's evil guardian is determined to have the gold mine for himself and his saloon-singer wife.
